"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The baseline scores 0.068 on 3 of 4 seeds and 0.258 on one, so runs are bimodal: most seeds get stuck in a weak optimum and a lucky one escapes. A 2-seed mean can move by about 0.1 from luck alone. The default recipe gives only 32 PPO updates (131k steps in batches of 4,096), which is very few for policy improvement. Two levers look most promising. First, more updates: smaller batches, or fewer epochs, which buys more samples. Second, a longer credit horizon (gamma 0.99), so the +1 exact-build bonus at episode end reaches early placements. With gamma 0.95 the bonus is discounted by about 0.95^15 ≈ 0.46 over a typical 8–20-brick episode. This round tests three recipe directions: fewer epochs for more data, smaller batches for more updates, and 1 epoch with a long horizon.
analyses.2: All three round-1 recipes gave exactly 0.0684 on both seeds, the same value as 3 of the 4 baseline seeds. Training success also stayed near 0.06–0.07. So the runs are stuck in one shared, repeatable local optimum, probably a near-deterministic policy that only solves the easy designs. Only one baseline seed escaped (0.258). Changing sample count (131k to 426k), update count (32 to 128), and horizon (gamma 0.99) did not move it. That points to early policy collapse or premature commitment, not data or horizon. The next tests should target exploration and optimisation stability: more entropy, a lower learning rate with more reuse, and denser short-horizon credit with less noisy advantages. A real escape should show up as at least one seed clearly above 0.07. Another 0.0684 on both seeds would rule out that lever.
analyses.3: All 8 seeds near the default recipe landed on exactly 0.0684 (35 of 512 designs). That is a stable local optimum, probably a simple strategy that only finishes the easiest designs. Changing epochs, batch size, gamma 0.99 or ent_coef 0.03 did not move it. Slowing learning hurt badly: lr 3e-4 with 8 epochs scored 0. Short horizon with ent_coef 0.02 scored 0.003. Only one default seed escaped, to 0.258, so escaping is possible but rare. Two settings have not been tried yet: faster learning (higher lr, wider clip) and less entropy. With hundreds of legal actions, an entropy bonus of 0.01 to 0.03 is large compared with per-step rewards of about 0.1. Since exact builds need precise placements, a weaker bonus may let the policy commit, while the evidence above suggests more entropy hurts. I test each lever alone on the default recipe and then together. A real gain should put both seeds clearly above 0.12.
analyses.4: Only one change worked: raising the learning rate to its 3e-3 cap (r3c1, mean 0.378, seeds 0.27 and 0.49), against a baseline of 0.116. Every other recipe stayed at the 0.068 optimum or fell to 0. Learning rate times gradient steps (updates × epochs × minibatches) seems to separate these runs. The default recipe takes 4,096 steps at 1e-3 (about 4.1) and r3c1 takes 4,096 at 3e-3 (about 12.3). The failed runs took 1,664 to 2,048 steps at 1e-3 or below (about 2 or less), except r3c3 (about 3.8, at 2e-3). Cutting epochs to buy more samples reduced the number of steps, so it failed. Low entropy (0.001) gave a small, noisy gain (0.093). The learning rate is already at its cap, so the next lever is more gradient steps at 3e-3: smaller minibatches or more, smaller updates. Gamma, lambda and higher entropy showed no benefit.
